Soap Opera Ratings Report For The Week Of October 19-23, 2026 (UPDATED)

How the four network soap operas performed among Total Viewers, Households, Women 18-49 and Women 25-54 Rating.
By Xavier ToupsNovember 1, 2026 11:31 PM Leave A Comment

“The Young and the Restless” continued to perform well in both Women 18-49 (0.29 rating) and Women 25-54 (0.47 rating), while “General Hospital” performed poorly in Women 18-49 (0.13 rating), ranking last in the key demo among soaps and across all of daytime broadcast, topped by “GMA3” (0.14 rating) and “NBC News Daily” (0.15 rating), with no preemptions or interruptions cited by Nielsen.

What follows is a breakdown of how the daytime soap operas performed during the week of October 19-23, 2026, in Total Viewers, Women 18-49 rating and Women 25-54 rating, including changes compared to Last Week (LW) and Last Year (LY).

Note: Starting with the 2025-2026 television season, Nielsen ratings are based on the Live+Same Day Big Data + Panel model.

An earlier version of this report included incorrect data among the Women 18-49 and Women 25-54 rankings, which have since been updated. The daily demo summary for each show remained correct.

***Please do not copy and paste the entire ratings. Thank you.***

LEGEND

About Nielsen Ratings

Rating: Estimated percentage of U.S. TV viewers (demographics, households, etc.) tuned in to a specific television program during an average minute.

Methods: As of September 22, 2025, the numbers above are calculated using Live+Same Day Big Data + Panel viewing and DVR playback, defined as 3:00 a.m. – 3:00 a.m., and are courtesy of Nielsen.

Starting in early 2026, Nielsen introduced the Advertising Research Foundation’s Latency Adjusted DASH UE (Universe Estimate) survey into its reporting, and as of August 31, 2026, the service has made “key enhancements” to improve its accuracy by correcting timing delays in survey data. Universe estimates are, as the name implies, an approximation of the total number of households or persons in a particular category – in this case, media consumption capabilities of U.S. homes. While previous DASH UEs were based on 2024 survey data, Nielsen is now updating them to reflect more recent trends in consumer behavior.  

Shift: Beginning August 31, 2020, national ratings include Out-of-Home (OOH) viewing. Previously, ratings did not include OOH viewing. Averages are based on regular telecasts.
